scenes.section: The US version: the main grouper families

lines.raw: The grouper families in one table.
lines.say: The grouper families in one table.

lines.raw: **DRG** (Diagnosis Related Group). What it groups (the unit): One inpatient hospital stay. Main use: Paying hospitals per stay; comparing stays. Common examples: MS-DRG (Medicare), APR-DRG (many Medicaid programmes). Where to learn it: Lesson 3.
lines.say: D R G (Diagnosis Related Group). What it groups (the unit): One inpatient hospital stay. Main use: Paying hospitals per stay; comparing stays. Common examples: M S DRG (Medicare), A P R DRG (many Medicaid programmes). Where to learn it: Lesson 3.

lines.raw: **APC** (Ambulatory Payment Classification). What it groups (the unit): Services in one hospital outpatient visit. Main use: Paying hospital outpatient departments. Common examples: Medicare OPPS APCs; EAPGs used by some Medicaid and commercial payers. Where to learn it: Lesson 4.
lines.say: A P C (Ambulatory Payment Classification). What it groups (the unit): Services in one hospital outpatient visit. Main use: Paying hospital outpatient departments. Common examples: Medicare O P P S A P C's; E A P G's used by some Medicaid and commercial payers. Where to learn it: Lesson 4.

lines.raw: **HCC** (Hierarchical Condition Category). What it groups (the unit): One member's diagnoses over a year. Main use: Risk adjustment: predicting next year's cost. Common examples: CMS-HCC (Medicare Advantage), HHS-HCC (ACA plans). Where to learn it: Risk Adjustment course.
lines.say: H C C (Hierarchical Condition Category). What it groups (the unit): One member's diagnoses over a year. Main use: Risk adjustment: predicting next year's cost. Common examples: C M S HCC (Medicare Advantage), H H S HCC (A C A plans). Where to learn it: Risk Adjustment course.

lines.raw: **Condition categories**. What it groups (the unit): Diagnosis codes (and the claims or members that have them). Main use: Counting illnesses; finding members with a chronic condition. Common examples: CCSR, chronic condition flags, comorbidity indexes. Where to learn it: Lesson 5.
lines.say: Condition categories. What it groups (the unit): Diagnosis codes (and the claims or members that have them). Main use: Counting illnesses; finding members with a chronic condition. Common examples: C C S R, chronic condition flags, comorbidity indexes. Where to learn it: Lesson 5.

lines.raw: **Episode groupers**. What it groups (the unit): All the care for one condition or procedure over a time window. Main use: Comparing total cost of a treatment; bundled payments. Common examples: Medicare episode definitions, commercial episode groupers. Where to learn it: Lessons 6 and 7.
lines.say: Episode groupers. What it groups (the unit): All the care for one condition or procedure over a time window. Main use: Comparing total cost of a treatment; bundled payments. Common examples: Medicare episode definitions, commercial episode groupers. Where to learn it: Lessons 6 and 7.
